Photograph: WA Police Indigenous Australians WA police appeal for help to find 10-year-old girl missing from Perth suburbs Lyndel Ningella was last seen leaving home in Butler on Saturday evening prompting concerns about her safety Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Sarah Collard Indigenous affairs correspondent Tue 18 Aug 2026 06.03 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 06.13 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Western Australia police have appealed for help in finding a 10-year-old girl who went missing from Perth’s outer northern suburbs on Saturday. Lyndel Ningella has not been seen since early Saturday evening when police said the young girl was seen leaving a home in Butler at about 5:45pm on 15 August. She was last seen wearing black shorts and a black jumper and is described as being about 160cm tall, of medium build and has long brown hair with blonde ends and dark brown eyes. Police believe that she may have travelled up to 80km away and could be in the Kwinana, Leda, Parmelia or Wellard areas of Perth’s coastal outer suburbs. WA police are requesting that anyone who sees Lyndel or has information regarding her whereabouts contact police immediately. Police had mistakenly alerted that she was located on Monday afternoon but several hours later they reissued an alert saying she was still missing. Asst Supt Darren Hart of Mandurah district police said he was concerned for her safety. “We hold concerns for Lyndel due to her young age and believe she may be staying with family and associates,” he said at a media conference. “It’s believed she may have travelled to the Wellard area and was possibly there across the weekend. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “We are concerned for her safety in that she is a 10-year-old girl who is making her own way in the world.” Explore more on these topics Indigenous Australians Australian police and policing Western Australia news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Morrison-era GST deal with WA a multi-billion dollar mistake that should be reversed, Productivity Commission finds Seven First Nations Australians tell us their worries and hopes for future generations – video Former Catholic bishop accused of hosting alcohol-fuelled parties to sexually abuse Aboriginal men found guilty First Nations woman reported DV concerns days before she was allegedly murdered by ex-partner, Queensland police say Perth teenager charged with murdering his mother and attempting to kill sister Victoria’s new First Nations body asks government to axe bill that will scrap prisoners’ ‘open air’ rights A poem by Ziggy Ramo: ‘A Welcome to Country was booed on Anzac Day. Photograph: Russell Freeman/AAP View image in fullscreen Emergency services at the scene of the Russell Island house fire. The blaze killed a father and five children. Photograph: Russell Freeman/AAP Queensland Mother flagged faulty smoke alarms before house fire that killed father and five children, court hears Pre-inquest conference into Queensland deaths hears witnesses did not hear any smoke alarms during 2023 fire Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Andrew Messenger Tue 8 Sep 2026 05.27 EDT Last modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 05.47 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A landlord was repeatedly warned about improperly installed smoke alarms before a house fire that killed a father and five children in Queensland in 2023, a coroner has heard. Deputy state coroner Donald MacKenzie held a pre-inquest conference into the Russell Island deaths on Tuesday. No witness recalls hearing the sound of an alarm during the blaze, it heard. The owner was fined $774 for improper installation in 2024, the maximum possible penalty under Queensland law. A conviction was not recorded. The fire in the two-storey wooden Queenslander broke out on 6 August 2023. The house had been moved to the island and then renovated in 2013 before being rented privately. Five children – two brothers aged four and others aged three, 10 and 11 – died in the blaze. Their father, 34, died after running into the fire to rescue them. None can be identified for legal reasons. The children’s mother and father had fallen asleep in a converted “chill out” area underneath the house. The father awoke to see thick black smoke and immediately raced upstairs, where the children were sleeping. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email His partner also tried to get into the house, but was forced back by the fire. Another adult woman leapt off a balcony to safety and survived. The Queensland fire department does not have a station on Russell Island, and vehicles must be ferried over in an emergency, a process that takes about 45-60 minutes, the court heard. As a result, it was a paramedic who first arrived at the scene, arriving within minutes at about 6.26am. “He recalls that the fire’s heat was so intense that he could feel it through his vehicle window, and could see the flames coming from the roof and smoke in a mushroom formation,” counsel assisting Corinne Leach told the court. “[The children’s mother] was kneeling on the ground in complete distress with [the other woman] beside her. He asked if anyone else was inside, to which [the mother} replied: her five children, and lost all ability to communicate.” The paramedic also tried to get into the building but was halted by the intense blaze. He instead focused on evacuating neighbouring homes. Rural firefighters arrived at 6.35am. The court heard the home had poor wiring, an exposed electrical box and faulty power points, known to short out. It also had an extension cord running from a poorly operating power point in a child’s bedroom, from a double adapter, to the understory area. The home’s smoke alarms also had not been updated in compliance with 2017 laws that applied to any tenancy renewed after January 2022 imposing additional safety measures for alarms. The homeowner claimed not to have been aware of the legislative change, the court heard. “[The mother] says that she raised the issue of non-working smoke alarms with the home’s owner, but nothing was done about it,” Leach told the court. “No witness recalls hearing a smoke alarm sounding at all prior or during the fire.” MacKenzie has been tasked with investigating seven issues, including whether legally installed fire alarms might have prevented the deaths, and whether the emergency service response to the fire was adequate. He will also consider whether the presence of any additional emergency service resources located on the island could have prevented the deaths. Fire investigators have been unable to identify the cause of the blaze, and could not categorically rule out that it was lit deliberately, the court heard. The inquest has been listed to sit for 10 days in November, to hear from 16 witnesses. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1kx.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Lil Durk holding the Grammy Award he won for best melodic rap performance in 2024 By Tinshui Yeung Published 1 hour ago Grammy-winning rapper Lil Durk was acquitted on Friday of all charges in a federal murder-for-hire case accusing him of orchestrating the revenge killing of a man shot dead in a daytime ambush in Los Angeles four years ago. The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo. Defence lawyer Drew Findling said the recording artist, whose real name is Durk Devontay Banks, was "thankful" following the verdict. Lil Durk has had seven albums in the US Billboard chart's top five since 2019 and has also collaborated with stars including Drake and J Cole on hit singles. Supporters cheered outside a Los Angeles courthouse after the verdict, which came following three days of jury deliberations. The 33-year-old faced five felony counts, including murder for hire resulting in death and conspiracy. If convicted, he could have faced a life sentence. Although Banks was found not guilty of the charges in the case, he remains in custody and faces a separate trial on 5 October, where he will face racketeering murder and firearms charges. "While we are disappointed with the jury's decision regarding Durk Banks, a.k.a. 'Lil Durk,' we look forward to presenting our evidence at his second trial", First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement. In the three-week trial, two co-defendants were tried alongside Banks. Deandre "OTF Dede" Wilson and David "Browneyez" Lindsey were convicted of stalking and conspiracy to commit stalking, but acquitted of murder-for-hire charges, the BBC's US partner CBS News reports , external . The trial relied on three co-operating witnesses, Kavon "OTF Vonnie" Grant, Keith "Flacka" Jones and Kacey "OTF Jam" Hester, who reached plea deals and testified against Banks, Wilson and Lindsey. It stemmed from a fatal shooting in August 2022 at a petrol station in Los Angeles, where a car carrying Rondo, whose real name is Tyquian Bowman, was shot at. Bowman was unharmed, but his cousin Saviay'a Robinson, who was also in the car, was killed. Federal prosecutors accused Banks of plotting to kill Bowman, in retaliation for the earlier murder of Chicago OTF rapper King Von, who was signed to OTF. Von was killed in 2020 during an early-morning exchange of gunfire in Atlanta. A friend of Bowman was charged with King Von's murder, but the charges were later dropped. Bowman was not arrested or charged. Authorities said Banks made it known that he would "pay a bounty" to anyone who killed Bowman. Prosecutors argued that Banks felt pressure on social media to avenge Von's death. Banks founded OTF in 2010. He won the 2024 Grammy Award for Best Melodic Rap Performance for his single "All My Life" featuring J Cole. He has also been nominated for a Grammy three other times. Weinstein, 74, forcibly performed oral sex in 2006 on Miriam Haley, one of dozens of women who have made accusations against the "Pulp Fiction" and "Shakespeare in Love" producer. Weinstein was sentenced to 23 years in 2020 for the sexual assault, but it was overturned on appeal in 2024. A jury found him guilty again in 2025 after a retrial in New York. He made a last-ditch plea for leniency Wednesday as he addressed a packed Manhattan court, where Haley sat in the audience. "I am not a violent man, have some mercy," said Weinstein, who wore a dark suit with a red tie and sat in a wheelchair due to health issues. "I sincerely apologize to anyone I have hurt," he added, while continuing to maintain his innocence during remarks met by loud groans inside the court. After sentencing, his spokesman Juda Engelmayer told AFP that Weinstein planned to appeal the latest sentence and conviction. "It is difficult to escape the conclusion that Harvey Weinstein is being sentenced not only for the crime of which he was convicted, but for who he is and what his name has come to represent," he said, referencing the #MeToo movement. 'Courage' Judge Curtis Farber slammed Weinstein as a "sexual predator" who had failed to take responsibility for his actions. "You had it all. Your legacy could have been cemented with greatness. But you threw it all away by assaulting Miriam Haley," Farber said. Prosecutors had sought 20 years in prison for Weinstein, while his lawyers warned that a longer sentence would likely see him die in prison. Haley said after the hearing that she believed the 15-year prison term "was fair, in my opinion. So I'm happy with it." She earlier told the court that she had suffered a "life sentence" and suffered post-traumatic stress disorder after Weinstein assaulted her in New York. She said that Weinstein "abused his position of power" and that she "felt embarrassed that he thought I was so insignificant that he dared to do something like this." Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg praised Haley for her "powerful, moving and eloquent" testimony in court. "I'm moved, as we should all be moved, by their courage and their steadfastness through what has obviously been a challenging process," he told reporters. MeToo movement Weinstein once ruled Hollywood as a kingpin powerful enough to make or break projects and careers. But investigations by The New Yorker and The New York Times exposed a raft of abusive behavior and prompted an avalanche of allegations from more than 80 people. Weinstein is also to be resentenced in California for the 2013 rape and assault of an actress in a Los Angeles hotel room, after an appeals court in June upheld the conviction but vacated his 16-year prison term. Meanwhile, a New York judge in May declared a mistrial in a separate case after jurors failed to reach a verdict on allegations he sexually assaulted actor Jessica Mann. It was the third time Mann had taken the stand against Weinstein after a 2020 guilty verdict was overturned due to mishandling of witnesses, and a 2025 case ended in mistrial after a jury-room feud. Prosecutors later said they would not pursue a fourth trial in Mann's case. Still, she attended the court Wednesday in support of Haley along with Polish-born actor Kaja Sokola – Weinstein was acquitted of sexual assault against her in a 2025 retrial. https://www.dw.com/en/ukrainian-presiden.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OLXI Zelenskyy, seen her with EU leaders Antonio Costa (left) and Ursula von der Leyen (right), made an impassioned plea for his country at the EU summit on Friday Image: Geert Vanden Wijngaert/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was applauded by EU leaders when he appeared at this week's summit in Brussels. But getting what he needs from Europe will be tough, and a public dispute with US President Donald Trump has put him in a very difficult position. Speaking to press at the summit, he said that "Putin wants to destroy us" and that Ukraine must prepare for a hard winter. Experts view the upcoming cold season as a rough one for Ukraine as well. "Ukraine is arguably entering the most difficult winter since [Russia's] full scale invasion ," Olena Prokopenko, a senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the United States, a nonpartisan think-tank, told DW. Three painful topics were on the table at the summit for discussion between Zelenskyy and EU leaders: US relations with Russia, Starlink ― and money. Is the US siding with Russia? Zelenskyy's visit to Brussels comes at a time when he needs European support more than ever. That's because his relationship with the US is worsening. Worries are growing in the EU and Ukraine that the US is growing more sympathetic to Russia. President Trump told US news channel Newsmax: "I think I find Zelenskyy to be more difficult to deal with than [Russian President Vladimir] Putin." Trump struck a deal to buy Russian diesel on October 12, which signifies a step back from sanctions placed on Russia and a blow for Ukraine. When Zelenskyy ordered Ukrainian forces to conduct fresh strikes on Russia's oil refineries , Trump labelled the Ukrainian leader's decision as "a disgrace." How Russia turned sanctions into a diesel deal To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video At the press conference at the summit on Friday, Zelenskyy told reporters that he knows that US-built missiles "are being sent to the Middle East, so it is no secret that we are not a priority." He is asking Europe instead to supply the military power Ukraine needs to get through the winter. Since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the US has been the biggest military donor to Ukraine. But the relationship between the two countries has become more difficult since the start of Donald Trump's second term in the White House. The Starlink slowdown Ukraine uses Starlink, a satellite Internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk . The country also uses Starshield, the military-grade version, for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones, though not for long-range strikes in Russia. At the summit, Zelenskyy spoke of his "deep and unpleasant" surprise upon finding out that Ukraine was experiencing disruptions to the systems . He said this has hobbled Ukraine's ability to defend itself. Both Elon Musk and the White House say they are not responsible for the slowdown. The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told the press at the summit before the talks began: "Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine and unfortunately in [the] short term Europe can't replace this capability." Prokopenko said that this was the reason "why Ukraine's most credible medium-term solution here is to continue relying on the US. And the EU is critical in this context in terms of backing Ukraine's requests for the US administration to keep those technologies on offer" for Kyiv. Speaking to journalists at the summit, Zelenskyy said the speed of Starlink had still not been fully restored but had improved. He said Ukraine is cooperating with various countries, including France, to search for a partial solution. Did someone order Ukraine's high-speed Starlink shutdown? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Ukraine's budget problem Zelenskyy urged EU leaders Friday to keep backing Kyiv financially as well, asking for nearly $80 billion (€70 billion) more next year. "This is a realistic amount and I ask you to find this support," Zelenskyy said. "It will help us hold Russia back." The EU gave Kyiv an approximately $100 billion (€90 billion) loan last year, making the EU Ukraine's biggest international backer. But the Ukrainian government is saying it needs more. "The war is becoming objectively more expensive, and the Ukrainian economy is increasingly affected by the Russian strikes, leading to a drastic decline in tax and customs revenues," Prokopenko said. "So the needs will continue growing." So will Ukraine get what it needs? Closing the summit, President of the European Council Antonio Costa said that Ukraine "remains a priority" and asked the European Commission to come up with a proposal to pull together more funds for the country in 2027. Essentially, it looks as though the EU will try to find a way to meet Ukraine's cash demands ― though it is not yet clear how. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen promised the EU will "continue to lead" but urged international partners to step up as well. Ukraine to 'keep living and fighting with dignity' Zelenskyy will leave Brussels without concrete promises or numbers, but with renewed commitments for support from Europe. The Ukrainian president concluded his press conference with an emotional statement: " We will keep living and fighting with dignity." https://dailycaller.com/2026/10/17/israe.text: Mark Tanos October 17, 2026 10:00 PM ET October 17, 2026 10:00 PM ET Mark Tanos Font Size: Masked Israeli settlers attacked a group of European diplomats touring the occupied West Bank on Saturday, leaving a French mayor beaten and a consular vehicle damaged. Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot said on X that the settlers went after Belgium’s consul general, French and Polish diplomats and Catholic representatives as they visited an olive harvest near the village of Taybeh. Prevot said his team was safe. 🇵🇸 I condemn in the strongest terms the attack by masked settlers in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank, against Palestinians, our Consul General, French and Polish diplomats as well as catholic representatives. A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged. Our team is safe. Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack. As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. Impunity for violent settlers must end. Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them. This violence cannot be separated from Israel’s illegal settlement policy. Belgium condemns settlement expansion and attempts to forcibly displace Palestinians from their land. The occupation of the Palestinian territory must end. @BelgiumMFA @BelgiumJRS — Maxime PREVOT (@prevotmaxime) October 17, 2026 Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, told Agence France-Presse that the attackers kicked him, struck him with iron bars and knocked him to the ground, CBS News reported . He said he escaped serious injury. “It’s the gratuitous nature of the violence that stuns me,” Baudoux said. “They arrived completely enraged.” (RELATED: ‘I’m Going To Die’: Video Shows Israeli Settlers Brutally Attacking WaPo Journalist, Beating Her With Clubs) Two Israeli activists at the scene told Israel National News that the masked men hemmed in their car and demanded identification. “The settlers blocked us, surrounded the vehicle, and demanded to see our identity cards. They told us they would kill us,” they said. Israel’s military denounced what it called a severe act of violence by Israeli rioters, while Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar said forensic teams had reached the site, Israel National News reported . “I strongly condemn the severe acts of violence by Israeli rioters in the area of Taybeh,” Sa’ar said. Police opened an investigation, though the army noted the visit had not been cleared with it beforehand. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office urged restraint before anyone assigned blame. “These reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge,” the office said. The Prime Minister’s Office: ALLEGED ATTACK ON EUROPEAN DIPLOMATS: SERIOUS ACCUSATIONS REQUIRE SERIOUS EVIDENCE. We urge caution before drawing conclusions from today’s reports that European diplomats were attacked by masked Israelis in Judea and Samaria. Any violence against diplomats is unacceptable. The more serious the accusation, the greater the demand for compelling evidence. Here is what we know: - The diplomatic delegation entered a sensitive area with a history of confrontations without prior coordination with the IDF, as officially confirmed by the military. Such coordination is essential to protecting visiting diplomats and preventing violence. - The visit included Bernard Baudoux, a French Communist Party mayor who previously raised the Palestinian flag over his municipal building, prompting French authorities to order its removal. - Published footage shows masked individuals confronting a diplomatic vehicle. Separate images show a smashed window and a person lying on the ground. These images alone do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility. Those circumstances remain under investigation. - Israeli police and forensic investigators have launched an investigation to establish the facts and identify those responsible. These reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge. We may see further allegations in the coming days. By the time the evidence is fully examined, the reputational damage from premature conclusions may already be done. We call on the public and responsible journalists to demand verifiable evidence, reject hearsay, and refuse to turn unproven allegations into a collective indictment of the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria. — Prime Minister of Israel (@IsraeliPM) October 17, 2026 Poland’s foreign ministry said its personnel were unharmed and saw no sign they had been singled out, according to CBS News. Prevot vowed to push for European Union sanctions.
